subject.title: [Bug]: CLI relay exits silently with code 1 when session lane is blocked — no timeout or busy error surfaced

question: Should same-session `openclaw agent` CLI lane waits become a terminal structured busy result, or should the CLI preserve eventual queued execution and only improve diagnostics?
rationale: Current main exposes the needed facts internally, but the candidate fix changes the user-visible delivery contract for blocked CLI dispatches and leaves exit-code behavior as a maintainer product/API choice.

options.title: Land a structured busy result
options.body: Repair and land the linked PR direction so CLI callers get actionable stderr/JSON for lane-busy waits while non-CLI Gateway calls stay unopted.

options.title: Keep queued execution and add diagnostics
options.body: Preserve existing eventual execution semantics and only add clearer CLI progress or timeout reporting, accepting less deterministic orchestration behavior.

options.title: Pause for broader queue policy
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide the larger lane-wait behavior across CLI, Gateway, and channel callers.

recommendation.title: Land a structured busy result
recommendation.body: Repair and land the linked PR direction so CLI callers get actionable stderr/JSON for lane-busy waits while non-CLI Gateway calls stay unopted.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits at the Gateway-backed agent CLI boundary introduced in steipete's earlier work and is a product/API contract choice more than a local queue-code fix.
